text:
alejandra (AE): Hi team — big POC with Acme Health is greenlit. They sent back an MSA with DPA and SLA redlines. Need legal + finance eyes before I reply.

Tom (SE): Can we confirm data residency clause? They want EU-only processing in prod.

alejandra (AE): Yes, initial POC will run on our eu-west region, but Contract wants both prod + backups restricted. Any blockers?

mike (Legal): Pulling up the PDF now. Main issues: 1) liability cap reduction request from $5M -> $15M; 2) deletion timeline in DPA changed to 10 business days; 3) SLA uptime target bumped to 99.99% with financial credits. I'll annotate.

sarah (Finance): Liability increase is a no-go without pricing changes or higher commitment. Can we propose a cap tied to annual spend instead of fixed number?

alejandra (AE): Customer is asking for signature before next Tue to meet procurement cycle. They're sensitive to timelines.

mike (Legal): Proposed counter: liability cap at 3x annual fees or $5M whichever is greater; deletion timeline 30 days standard, 15 for urgent cases; SLA 99.9% with a maximum service credit of 10% monthly invoice. Will draft redlines and share.

procurement-bot: Uploaded: acme_msa_v2_redlines.pdf

Tom (SE): Question on DPA: they ask for access to production logs. We should never provide raw prod logs. Can we offer scoped, redacted logs or aggregated metrics instead?

mike (Legal): Agree. Offer redacted logs + SOC2 report and optional scoped audit in-person under NDA.

june (customer-procurement): @alejandra thanks. Our security team really needs the 15 day deletion window. Can you confirm we can get that in writing?

alejandra (AE): @june I can try but legal needs to balance. Mike proposing 15 for urgent, 30 for standard. Is that acceptable if we put 'urgent' definition in SOW?

june (customer-procurement): Yes if 'urgent' is defined and limited, we can accept.

sarah (Finance): Also, order form needs to reflect committed monthly minimum to qualify for the proposed liability formula. What number do we put?

alejandra (AE): They want a flexible start: POC month then scale. Can we do a 3-month committed minimum of $40k/mo? Customer prefers not to lock long term.

sarah (Finance): 3 months at $40k is borderline. If we accept lower cap liability formula tied to annualized run rate, we need a higher commit. Alternative: agree to 3-month pilot at promo rate but exclude pilot from liability calculation.

mike (Legal): Noted. I'll insert language: 'Pilot period excluded from annualized spend calculation for liability cap.'

procurement-bot: Order form draft uploaded: acme_orderform_2024-03.docx

alejandra (AE): Next step: Mike to upload redlined MSA + DPA by EOD, Sarah to propose order form with two options (3-month pilot vs 12-month commit), Tom to prepare tech appendix about log access and EU processing.

mike (Legal): Uploaded: acme_msa_redlined_171212.pdf

sarah (Finance): Uploaded: acme_orderform_options.csv

Tom (SE): Uploaded: acme_tech_appendix.md

june (customer-procurement): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Once we see the redlines we'll route internally. Can you share signature routing expectations?

alejandra (AE): We'll accept e-signature via DocuSign. For enterprise we need PO first for onboarding. We'll send invoice upon signature per the order form terms.

june (customer-procurement): OK — procurement will aim for PO after legal clears. Timeline target: PO within 5 business days of final MSA.

mike (Legal): I'll try to finalize redlines tomorrow morning. If customer counters again, we'll set up 20-min call to close remaining points.

alejandra (AE): Thanks everyone. I'll keep customer posted. :thumbsup:

procurement-bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up in 48h.
